title: Benchmark — Premium SSD v1 vs v2
description: Side-by-side comparison of two benchmark runs. Selecting the runs rather than filtering by time is deliberate: the two runs happen at different wall-clock times, so a shared time axis would show one run or the other, never both. This dashboard is fed exclusively by the Layer 2 collector, because Premium SSD v2 is in preview and Azure platform metrics may be incomplete for it.

query.query: MysqlMetrics | summarize LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by RunId | order by LastSeen desc | project RunId
MysqlMetrics | summarize LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by RunId | order by LastSeen desc | project RunId

panels.title: Headline comparison
panels.description: Avg / p95 / max for the metrics that decide the storage question. p95 matters more than avg here: a gaming workload feels tail latency, not the mean.

targets.query:
let metrics = dynamic(['Innodb_data_reads', 'Innodb_data_writes', 'Innodb_data_fsyncs', 'Innodb_os_log_fsyncs', 'Innodb_row_lock_time_avg', 'Innodb_log_waits', 'Threads_running', 'Slow_queries']);
MysqlMetrics
| where RunId in ('$baseline', '$candidate')
| where Metric in (metrics)
| summarize Avg = round(avg(Value), 2), P95 = round(percentile(Value, 95), 2), Max = round(max(Value), 2), Samples = count() by Metric, RunId, Tier
| order by Metric asc, RunId asc

panels.title: Delta — candidate vs baseline
panels.description: Positive PercentChange means the candidate run recorded a higher value. Whether higher is better depends on the metric: more IOPS is good, more log waits is not.

targets.query:
let metrics = dynamic(['Innodb_data_reads', 'Innodb_data_writes', 'Innodb_data_fsyncs', 'Innodb_os_log_fsyncs', 'Innodb_row_lock_time_avg', 'Innodb_log_waits', 'Threads_running', 'Slow_queries']);
MysqlMetrics
| where RunId in ('$baseline', '$candidate')
| where Metric in (metrics)
| summarize P95 = percentile(Value, 95) by Metric, RunId
| summarize Baseline = anyif(P95, RunId == '$baseline'), Candidate = anyif(P95, RunId == '$candidate') by Metric
| where isnotnull(Baseline) and isnotnull(Candidate) and Baseline > 0
| extend PercentChange = round(100.0 * (Candidate - Baseline) / Baseline, 1)
| order by abs(PercentChange) desc

panels.title: Data read rate — elapsed seconds into run
panels.description: The x-axis is seconds since each run started, not wall-clock time, so two runs recorded hours apart overlay cleanly.

targets.query:
let runStarts = MysqlMetrics | where RunId in ('$baseline', '$candidate') | summarize RunStart = min(Timestamp) by RunId;
MysqlMetrics
| where RunId in ('$baseline', '$candidate')
| where Metric == 'Innodb_data_reads'
| order by RunId asc, Timestamp asc
| extend PrevValue = prev(Value), PrevTs = prev(Timestamp), PrevRun = prev(RunId)
| where RunId == PrevRun
| extend Seconds = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, PrevTs)
| where Seconds > 0 and Value >= PrevValue
| extend Rate = (Value - PrevValue) / Seconds
| join kind=inner runStarts on RunId
| extend ElapsedSeconds = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, RunStart)
| project ElapsedSeconds, RunId, Rate
| order by ElapsedSeconds asc

targets.query:

MysqlMetrics

| order by RunId asc, Timestamp asc

panels.title: Run inventory
panels.description: Confirms the two runs are actually comparable — a run with far fewer samples or a much shorter duration did not exercise the server the same way.

targets.query:
MysqlMetrics
| summarize Started = min(Timestamp), Ended = max(Timestamp), Samples = count(), Metrics = dcount(Metric) by RunId, Tier, Host
| extend DurationMinutes = round(datetime_diff('second', Ended, Started) / 60.0, 1)
| order by Started desc
